title: Java Fundamentals
description: Core Java concepts: OOP, immutability, memory, collections, and exception handling.

questions.question: Which keyword is used in Java to prevent a method from being overridden by subclasses?
questions.explanation: The 'final' keyword prevents a method from being overridden and a class from being inherited.

questions.question: In Java, String objects are immutable, meaning their state cannot be changed after creation.
questions.explanation: True! String is immutable. Any modification method (like concat, replace) returns a new String instance.

questions.question: Fill in the blank for the standard entry point method signature in Java:
questions.explanation: The main method does not return any value, so its return type must be 'void'.

questions.question: What is the default value of an uninitialized instance boolean variable in Java?
questions.explanation: Instance and static boolean variables in Java default to 'false'. Local variables have no default.

questions.question: A Java class can directly extend multiple classes simultaneously (multiple inheritance with classes).
questions.code:
// Is this allowed?
class C extends A, B { }
questions.explanation: False! Java does not support multiple class inheritance to avoid the diamond problem. However, a class can implement multiple interfaces.

questions.question: What keyword is used by a class to inherit another class in Java?
questions.explanation: The 'extends' keyword is used for class inheritance (or interface extending another interface).

questions.question: Which of the following Collections maintains insertion order and allows duplicate elements?
questions.explanation: ArrayList is an ordered List implementation that preserves insertion order and allows duplicate elements.

questions.question: In Java, the '==' operator compares object reference (memory address), while .equals() compares logical values (if overridden).
questions.explanation: True! '==' checks whether both references point to the exact same object in memory, while .equals() checks logical equality.

questions.question: Which block in Java exception handling will execute regardless of whether an exception occurred or was caught?
questions.explanation: The 'finally' block always executes after try/catch, typically used to clean up resources like closing streams or database connections.

questions.question: Which access modifier allows access within the same package AND by subclasses in different packages?
questions.explanation: 'protected' grants access to members within the same package and to subclasses even if they reside in different packages.
